title: Lighthouse Watch Chronicle
premise: A coastal inheritance spanning decades. Human-readable context only; never fed to the SUT.

states.middle_aged_sturdy: A lighthouse keeper in his fifties, gray-white beard, thick deep-green waterproof coat and tall rubber boots, rough calloused hands, sturdy frame and steady stride, eyes distant and weary.
states.cane_twilight: The same keeper in old age: hair and beard fully white, face gaunt and sunken, stooped and walking slowly with a wooden cane, still in that faded deep-green old coat.
states.deceased: The lighthouse keeper has closed his eyes in death, lying still, face peaceful, no breath left.

states.youth: Young Mara: a lean fisher girl of fourteen or fifteen, deep-blue headscarf, coarse cotton fishing clothes, bright stubborn eyes.
states.adult: Adult Mara: a tall steady fisherwoman in her twenties, still in that deep-blue headscarf and coarse cotton fishing clothes, eyes bright and firm.

states.intact: A thick old ledger, corners capped in polished brass, deep-brown leather cover intact, yellowed pages packed with ink.
states.salt_weathered: The same ship's log salt-bleached by sea wind: cover whitened and curling, pages damp and wrinkled, writing bled.

states.intact_rotating: A man-tall rotating Fresnel lens of intact concentric glass prism rings, turning at even speed, refracting a sharp white beam.
states.cracked: The same Fresnel lens burst with glaring cracks, some glass prism rings damaged, the rotating beam broken by gaps.
states.repaired: The Fresnel lens cracks filled with newly set glass prism rings, restored intact, the beam sharp and steady again.

states.intact: A small indigo wooden fishing boat, a white petrel with spread wings painted on the bow, old tire fenders hanging along the gunwales.
states.sunk: The indigo fishing boat overturned by a giant wave, mast snapped, wreckage sinking into the surf.

states.youth: Young Lena: twin sister nearly identical in face to young Mara, ochre-red wool shawl, bold expression, a shell hairpin at her temple.
states.adult: Adult Lena: nearly identical in face to adult Mara, still in ochre-red shawl with shell hairpin at the temple, bold expression.

E7.name: lighthouse
E7.appearance: A white granite lighthouse standing on a black rocky headland, tall and slender, glass lantern room at the top, sea fog year-round.

E8.name: lantern room
E8.appearance: The circular glass lantern room atop the lighthouse, brass railings around, Fresnel lens in the center, endless sea beyond the windows.

E9.name: rocky shore
E9.appearance: The black rocky shore at the lighthouse foot, breaking waves, scattered old fishing nets, glass floats, and driftwood.

E10.name: fishing village market
E10.appearance: An open-air market in the small fishing village across the bay, fish baskets and salted fish under wooden sheds, nets on drying lines, people coming and going.

E11.name: memorial plaque
E11.appearance: A brass memorial plaque nailed to a granite base, engraved with the keeper's name and years, edges already verdigrised.

E12.name: glass floats
E12.appearance: Three palm-sized old glass floats, frosted with salt, tied with hemp rope to a wooden stake on the rocky shore.

E13.name: Seagull
E13.appearance: A brand-new vermilion motor rescue boat, white 'Seagull' lettering sprayed on the hull, orange life rings hung on the rail.

E14.name: harbor master
E14.appearance: A lean harbor master, full beard, deep-blue uniform coat and peaked cap, crisp bearing, somewhat resembling the lighthouse keeper.

E15.name: spare oil lamps
E15.appearance: A row of five brass spare oil lamps hung on iron hooks on the lantern-room wall, glass covers polished bright.

E16.name: brass fog bells
E16.appearance: Two brass fog bells hung under the lighthouse eaves, bodies faintly gleaming, low-toned fog warnings when the wind rises.

E17.name: Sara
E17.appearance: A fisher girl from across the bay, light-brown headscarf, dusty coarse cloth clothes; at a glance somewhat like young Mara, but sharper chin and shy gaze.

E18.name: spare prism
E18.appearance: A half-man-tall spare prism, concentric glass rings much like the main lens, but smaller, with a black-iron base.

E19.name: new fishing boat
E19.appearance: A strange blue-gray motor fishing boat, broad flat hull, no petrel emblem, not the same as the Petrel.

segments.action: At dusk, lighthouse keeper Elias climbs the spiral iron stair into the lantern room and lights the central Fresnel lens.
A row of five brass spare oil lamps hangs on the lantern-room wall; Elias polishes each glass cover one by one.
Two brass fog bells hang under the lighthouse eaves; Elias reaches out and lets them ring gently.
Elias circles the Fresnel lens, checking every glass prism ring.
Elias looks out the window at the darkening sea.
The Fresnel lens rotates at even speed, casting a white beam toward the night sea.
Elias sits in a lantern-room corner and dozes by the light.
Elias opens the ship's log and dips ink to record the day's tides.
Elias draws a wave-height curve in the ship's log.
Elias closes the ship's log and returns it to the wooden box by the brass railing.
The Fresnel lens beam sweeps the lantern room, lighting Elias's profile.
On the morning rocky shore, Elias greets young Mara as she poles the indigo Petrel to shore.
Mara jumps down from the Petrel and ties the hawser to the rocks.
Elias points to the three glass floats tied to the wooden stake, teaching Mara to read the fishing season.
Mara crouches by a tidal pool on the rocky shore, studying the anemones with curiosity.
Elias points at the sea, explaining the current's path to Mara.
Mara looks back at the moored Petrel, eyes full of longing.
In the noisy fishing village market, Lena in an ochre-red shawl turns to look from behind a fish shed.

segments.action: The Fresnel lens beam sweeps slowly through the mist.
Seasons turn; day after day Elias climbs to the lantern room to light the lamp.
Another snowy night, Elias wraps his coat tight and keeps watch beside the Fresnel lens.
In spring fishing season, Elias watches returning boat lights from the lantern-room window.
At midsummer noon, Elias wipes the brass railings heated by the fierce sun.
Autumn fog thickens; the Fresnel lens beam struggles through the mist in the lantern room.
Another New Year's Eve, Elias keeps watch alone in the lantern room until dawn.
At dawn, Elias patrols the rocky shore; the indigo Petrel lies in the shallow bay.
Elias crouches to check the seams of the Petrel's hull.
Elias walks to the wooden stake; those three glass floats are still tied on the rocky shore.
A strange blue-gray new fishing boat passes the shallow bay—broad flat hull, not Elias's Petrel.
Elias stands on the rocky shore, logging the reefs exposed after the ebb.
Elias hangs fishing nets on wooden racks on the rocky shore.
A storm rises suddenly; the lantern room shudders in the gale; the Fresnel lens shakes hard.
Wild waves pound; lantern-room glass reflects pale lightning.
Thunder cracks; a glaring crack bursts across the Fresnel lens.

The damaged Fresnel lens still turns slowly with its crack; the beam has a gap.

segments.action: A vermilion Seagull enters the shallow bay, nothing like the long-sunk Petrel.
A full-bearded harbor master jumps onto the rocky shore and talks beside Elias; the two are similar in build.
The harbor master points at the vermilion Seagull, explaining the new patrol plan to Elias.
The Seagull sounds its horn and leaves; Elias alone on the rocky shore watches it go.
From across the bay comes fisher girl Sara in a light-brown headscarf; at a glance she somewhat resembles Mara of those years.
Sara practices tying a hawser on the rocks; Elias shakes his head—she is not Mara after all.
Years later at dusk, fully white-haired Elias leans on a wooden cane, stooped beneath the white granite lighthouse.
